source_metadata.title: Silent Hypoxia in COVID-19: A Case Series

consistency_findings: Narrative/abstract defines silent hypoxemia as Borg CR10 >=5, while Table 2 labels Borg >=5 as dyspnea; this is directionally inconsistent with silent/less dyspnea.
Discussion states COVID-19 patients had higher dyspnea sensation, while abstract/results/Figure 1 show lower Borg ratings in COVID-19.
Narrative reports OR 0.221 (95% CI 0.054-0.907; p=0.036) attributed to COVID-19 and severe hypocapnia, but Table 2 does not directly contain that estimate.
Non-COVID AECOPD count is 15/37 (41%) in narrative/abstract but Table 1 lists AECOPD as main diagnosis in 13/37 (35%); Table 1 separately lists COPD comorbidity in 15/37 (41%).
Table 2 uses N=78 rather than the full N=82 without an explicit missing-data explanation.
The confidence interval for pH <7.35 in Table 2 is printed ambiguously as 1.744-5,263-453 and was not normalized.
extraction_limitations: No supplement was present in the retrieved source folder.
Bibliography entries were not atomized; references are provenance infrastructure under the ATOM protocol.
Figure 1 provides boxplots but not exact subgroup quartiles in text; subgroup atoms preserve only the source-supported direction and p value.
No source details were invented to reconcile internal inconsistencies.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated internal-source-inconsistency atom kind; three inconsistencies are represented as atom_kind=other with descriptive tags.
